standard.title: Evaluate and refine drama
standard.description: evaluate and refine use of elements of drama and/or conventions to shape and sustain dramatic action and/or communicate ideas, perspectives and/or meaning
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can make basic evaluations of own drama work (AC9ADR6C02). They have not yet systematically evaluated element and convention choices against intended dramatic purpose, or used that evaluation to make and document specific refinements.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students evaluate and refine use of elements and conventions through deliberate questioning, feedback and reflection to shape dramatic action and communicate intended meaning.

nodes.label: Evaluating element and convention choices
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can evaluate their use of elements and conventions against intended dramatic purpose and identify specific refinements
nodes.minimum_width: Evaluate at least one element or convention in own drama against the intended purpose; identify at least one specific refinement and explain why it improves the drama
nodes.typical_width: Evaluate use of elements, conventions and design choices against dramatic intent; use Viewpoints questions to interrogate own choices; identify and document specific refinements with reasoning
wider: Use Viewpoints questions systematically to evaluate own drama — 'What are your intentions?', 'Is meaning clear?', 'How could elements be used differently?' — document what each question reveals about gaps between intention and execution
Evaluate how costume, props and setting contribute to dramatic meaning — assess whether design choices support or undermine the intended effect
Evaluate how empathy is built into the dramatic experience — assess whether character portrayal and dramatic choices treat subjects with the care they deserve

response_modes.reason: Students commonly evaluate drama as 'good' or 'needs work' without specifying what element or convention choice is at issue and why. Scaffolding the evaluation (what is the intention, which element or convention serves that intention, does the current choice achieve it, what specific change would improve it?) builds targeted evaluation rather than general impression.

success_criteria: Evaluates at least one element or convention against intended purpose
Identifies at least one specific refinement with a reason — not just 'make it better'
Evaluation is connected to dramatic intent, not just personal preference

nodes.label: Refining drama through rehearsal
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can use the rehearsal process to refine dramatic action, adjusting element and convention choices based on evaluation and feedback
nodes.minimum_width: Make at least one documented refinement to drama during rehearsal based on evaluation or feedback; explain what changed and why
nodes.typical_width: Use rehearsal as an iterative refinement process; plan, organise and rehearse dramatic action; document decisions about elements, conventions and design; evaluate progress toward intended effect
wider: Adjust performance based on audience response — evaluate how audience feedback reveals the gap between intention and reception
Plan and organise the use of available theatre technologies in rehearsal — evaluate how each production decision supports or changes the dramatic meaning
Develop a rehearsal structure that systematically addresses specific dramatic challenges — evaluate the effectiveness of the structure against the intended dramatic purpose

response_modes.reason: Productive rehearsal — making targeted refinements, iterating based on evaluation, building toward a sustained dramatic effect — is a disciplined practice that develops through repeated cycles. Students who rehearse once without targeted refinement don't develop the rehearsal habit that makes drama improve over time.

success_criteria: Makes at least one documented refinement during rehearsal
Explains what changed and why — not just 'I practised it more'
Refinement is targeted — connected to a specific element, convention or dramatic intention

nodes.label: Sustaining dramatic action with coherent intent
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can evaluate and refine drama to sustain dramatic action and communicate intended ideas, perspectives and meaning throughout a complete work
nodes.minimum_width: Perform or present a drama and evaluate whether intended meaning was communicated; identify at least one aspect of element or convention use that would change in a future version
nodes.typical_width: Stage devised or scripted drama for a clear and intended purpose; evaluate whether the overall structure and use of elements and conventions sustained the dramatic action and communicated intended meaning throughout
wider: Consider how and why empathy should be built into the entire dramatic experience — evaluate whether empathy is maintained through all dramatic choices, not just in individual moments
Explore conventions for developing characters and stories from diverse cultures — evaluate how these conventions build empathy and cultural understanding for audiences
Reflect on whether the drama's overall structure and choices communicated intended ideas with clarity — evaluate both what worked and what the audience actually received

response_modes.reason: This node integrates evaluation of elements and conventions (Node 1), rehearsal refinement (Node 2), and performance skills from D01 into a coherent evaluation of a complete dramatic work. Students who can evaluate individual moments but cannot assess whether the whole drama sustained its intent have not met the standard's demand.

success_criteria: Evaluates whether intended meaning was communicated in a complete drama
Identifies at least one specific aspect that would change in a future version with reasoning
Evaluation addresses the whole work — not just isolated moments
